correctness.rationale: For finite positive target strength, the exact renewal MFPT diverges at r->0 and r->infinity. In the y=w-m variable, derivative numerator N/y^2 has strictly positive derivative: negative reciprocal terms and positive-series tails establish a single transverse crossing for all m>0; a separate positive-series derivative works at m=0. Exact orientation identity implies strict all-magnitude order. Coercive compactness plus a uniform C^1 expansion in 1/m at the limiting nondegenerate minimum y=1 proves z_+^2=2m+O(1/m), z_-^2=2m-2/(e eta)+O(1/m), hence the claimed physical offset. Reproducible standard-library finite tests: 1386 assertions, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The first-published formula and weak-drift response are already in Mazzolo (2026), and are not claimed as new. The newly evaluated claim combines proof of a unique nondegenerate optimum for every finite drift and finite reactivity, global strict directional ordering, and a nonzero constant asymptotic difference kappa/(e ell) at strong drift. value.rationale: The model has competing drift advection, resetting and finite local-time absorption; global optimizer uniqueness and orientation ordering remove protocol-design ambiguity at arbitrary drift. At strong drift, the exact nonzero subleading gap kappa/(e ell) isolates a physically meaningful reaction-limited direction effect not captured by leading drift scaling. It also identifies singular order of limits with perfect absorption. This is a motivated quantitative theorem rather than an arbitrary fitted constant.
